title: feat(ui): render sidebar and chat from cached state before the Gateway connects

commit.messageHeadline: feat(ui): persist agent roster boot record
feat(ui): cache sidebar roster in IndexedDB
feat(ui): render warm shell before the gateway connects
test(ui): prove warm reload and cursor reconciliation
docs(web): describe warm reload
fix(ui): retire warm caches when credentials change
fix(ui): wait for the stored transcript before the first startup request
fix(ui): flush the boot record on page hide
fix(ui): skip the transcript wait when startup is already at hand
perf(ui): prewarm the routed transcript snapshot at boot
fix(ui): prewarm the transcript through the light snapshot reader
fix(ui): clear boot records synchronously when credentials change
fix(ui): clear boot records synchronously on profile mismatch
test(ui): reconcile warm proof fixtures with main
perf(ui): defer the roster cache reader off the boot path
fix(ui): keep Incognito sessions out of the roster cache
fix(ui): release the roster wait when the Gateway becomes ready
test(ui): keep the roster-wait release probe out of the promise executor
feat(gateway): report the authentication method in hello
fix(ui): bind warm boot to the browser-held credential
docs(web): scope warm reload to browser-held credentials
test(ui): keep unrelated test lanes as on main
fix(ui): keep connected short-id loads on the Gateway resolver
test(gateway): expect the hello auth method in the reused-grant shape
chore(ui): re-baseline Control UI startup JS budget to 351659 B
fix(ui): seed the persisted Gateway token in warm-boot tests

Thanks for the review. Disposition of the findings against the rebased head (the reviewed head `a05df90ef92` predates the rebase onto current `main`):

- **[P1] Exclude Incognito sessions before persisting the roster** — accepted and fixed. `isPersistableSessionRow` now filters `incognito: true` rows at the write boundary (`session-roster-cache.runtime.ts`) and again on restore (`session-roster-cache.reader.ts`), so a record written by an older writer cannot resurface them; the regression test covers both boundaries. The transcript snapshot store is unchanged by this PR and already predates it.
- **[P2] Release the roster wait when the Gateway becomes ready** — accepted and fixed. `whenCachedRosterSettled` now races the IndexedDB read against Gateway readiness (and disposal); a late read still cannot publish cached rows after retirement. Regression test added.
- **[P2] Provide the required boot record in the sidebar fixtures** — fixed during the rebase (`test(ui): reconcile warm proof fixtures with main`); the fixtures now pass a boot record and the separate no-record admission test remains.
- **[P2] Validate short-link destinations beyond the cached subset** — not taken. Cached short-id resolution requires a unique match on the URL's short id (at least 8 hex characters of the trailing UUID) plus, when present, the slug, within the same 200-row primary page the in-memory sidebar roster already uses for the identical purpose on in-app navigation (`findUiSessionRow`); a wrong destination requires a second session whose UUID shares that prefix, which is a 2^-32 event per candidate. A stale cached row that no longer exists on the Gateway yields an empty transcript and is replaced by the live roster on hello. Keeping the same semantics for reload as for in-app navigation is deliberate; a post-hello `sessions.resolve` cross-check would add a round trip to every warm reload for that probability.
- **Merge risks** — the conflicts are resolved by the rebase (head now applies cleanly on `main`). The two captures are fixture-only (isolated Gateway, mock provider, UUID-named seeded sessions); they were inspected before upload. Compatibility with an existing browser profile: both stores are additive (`openclaw.control.bootRecord.v1:*` in localStorage, IndexedDB `openclaw-session-roster` v1) with versioned records that are removed on any shape mismatch, so a profile without them boots exactly as today, and credential change or a mismatching profile on hello clears them synchronously before the lazy IndexedDB cleanup.
- **Decision needed** — the bounded cache design (retention, pre-hello visibility, clearing, upgrade behavior) is the maintainer's accepted design: it was specified by the maintainer before implementation and this PR lands it on the maintainer's instruction.

Follow-up on the remaining item and on a new finding from the independent review of this head:

- **Data-model compatibility proof** — recorded in the PR body under Evidence ("Upgrade compatibility"). Both stores are additive and versioned: boot records carry a `version` field and any record that fails validation is removed on read (a version-1 record from the earlier revision of this branch costs one cold boot), the IndexedDB roster database is version 1 with per-record validation and eviction bounds, and the transcript snapshot store is unchanged by this PR. A browser profile without either store boots exactly as today. `ui/src/app/boot-record.test.ts` covers version and fingerprint rejection.
- **Identity binding (new, from autoreview)** — under trusted-proxy or Tailscale authentication a user switch on the same browser profile leaves the Gateway URL and stored credentials unchanged, so the previous user's cached roster could have rendered before hello. Fixed: hello-ok now reports `auth.method`, warm state is written only for `token` and `device-token` connections and is bound to a fingerprint of the credential that authenticated, and boot accepts a record only when the credential the browser can present matches. Proxy, Tailscale, password, and bootstrap identities persist nothing; the e2e suite has a trusted-proxy scenario proving the cold path.

Merged via squash.
